title: Four fifths or seven ninths: which is greater?
description: Four fifths and seven ninths are hard to compare directly. The board finds a common multiple of five and nine, writes both fractions with it, and compares the top numbers. Keeko doubts the answer by saying the fraction with the bigger bottom number is bigger.
teaching_notes: One idea: find a common multiple of the two bottom numbers, rewrite both fractions with it, and compare the top numbers. Watch for students who think a bigger bottom number means a bigger fraction.

video_script.why: A learner compares two fractions with different bottom numbers by finding a common multiple of the bottom numbers.
video_script.substitution: the book's own pair four fifths and seven ninths
video_script.anchor: the pair four fifths and seven ninths as two bars of the same length
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says seven ninths is bigger because nine is a bigger number than five, forgetting that ninths are smaller pieces than fifths.
video_script.payoff_line: four fifths is greater than seven ninths

final_answer.spoken: four fifths is thirty-six forty-fifths and seven ninths is thirty-five forty-fifths, so four fifths is greater than seven ninths

video_script.fraction_reading: four fifths, seven ninths, thirty-six forty-fifths, thirty-five forty-fifths
never_show: a tick on 7/9 before the working
maths_rules: 5 x 9 = 45, and 45 is a common multiple of 5 and 9
slip: Keeko says 7/9 is bigger because 9 is bigger than 5; but a ninth is a smaller piece than a fifth, and 7/9 = 35/45 < 36/45
video_script.design: Two bars of the same length, one cut in fifths and one in ninths. The two bottom numbers give forty-five, and the top numbers thirty-six and thirty-five are compared.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; two bars of the same length, one cut in fifths with four parts shaded and one cut in ninths with seven parts shaded; the shaded ends look close; the words which is greater? appear

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.bars: two bars of the same length appear, cut in fifths and in ninths, with four parts and seven parts shaded
marks.ask: the words which is greater? appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book. It can be difficult to compare two such fractions directly.
<bookmark mark='bars'/>One bar shows four fifths, and the other shows seven ninths.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which is greater, four fifths or seven ninths?

beats.on_screen: the two bars hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the bottom numbers 5 and 9 are circled in different colours; the multiples of 5 and the multiples of 9 are listed and 45 appears in both lists and is circled

marks.units: the bottom numbers 5 and 9 are circled in different colours with the note different fractional units
marks.multiples: the multiples of 5 and of 9 are listed, and 45 appears in both lists and is circled with the label common multiple

narration: <bookmark mark='units'/>Fifths and ninths are pieces of different sizes. We want a bottom number that both five and nine reach.
<bookmark mark='multiples'/>A number that is a multiple of both is called a common multiple.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the two fractions are four fifths and seven ninths.

beats.on_screen: To find: which fraction is greater
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find which of the two fractions is greater.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 5 x 9 = 45; 45 is a common multiple of 5 and 9; use 45 as the bottom number

marks.cm: 5 x 9 = 45 is written and 45 is circled
marks.use: the words use 45 as the common bottom number are written

narration: <bookmark mark='cm'/>Step one, five times nine is forty-five. Forty-five is a common multiple of five and nine.
<bookmark mark='use'/>Both fractions can be written with forty-five as the bottom number.

marks.mul: the top and the bottom of 4/5 are multiplied by 9

narration: <bookmark mark='mul'/>Step two, multiply the top and the bottom of four fifths by nine.
<bookmark mark='res'/>Four times nine over five times nine is thirty-six forty-fifths.

marks.mul: the top and the bottom of 7/9 are multiplied by 5

narration: <bookmark mark='mul'/>Step three, multiply the top and the bottom of seven ninths by five.
<bookmark mark='res'/>Seven times five over nine times five is thirty-five forty-fifths.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: both in forty-fifths; compare the numbers of forty-fifths: 36 and 35

marks.cmp: 36 forty-fifth pieces and 35 forty-fifth pieces are lined up one above the other

narration: <bookmark mark='cmp'/>Step four, both fractions are counted in the same unit, so we compare the top numbers. One has thirty-six, and the other has thirty-five.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Thirty-six is more than thirty-five, so four fifths is greater than seven ninths.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the two bars
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says 7/9 is bigger because 9 is bigger than 5; one fifth and one ninth of the same bar are laid side by side and the ninth is shorter; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: the bubble with the wrong idea appears
marks.pieces: one fifth and one ninth of the same bar are laid side by side, and the ninth is shorter
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and 35/45 < 36/45 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks seven ninths is bigger, because nine is a bigger number than five.
<bookmark mark='pieces'/>But a bigger bottom number cuts the bar into smaller pieces. A ninth is shorter than a fifth.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>We still need one common unit before we can compare.
